video.title: Async Property, Async Throws & Async Initializer | Day 271
video.description:
Learn to explain how to talk about code that waits when you read a property, call a function or create a value: Async Property, Async Throws & Async Initializer, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Async Property - A read-only property whose getter is marked async, so you must await it.
Async Throws - Two keywords that mark a function that can both suspend and fail, so callers write try await.
Async Initializer - An initializer marked async, so creating the value can wait for work and needs await.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Async Property, Async Throws & Async Initializer in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Async Property, Async Throws, Async Initializer 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Async Property - A read-only property whose getter is marked async, so you must await it.
한국어: Async Property: getter가 async라서 읽을 때 await가 필요한 읽기 전용 프로퍼티

Async Throws - Two keywords that mark a function that can both suspend and fail, so callers write try await.
한국어: Async Throws: 일시 중단도 되고 에러도 던질 수 있는 함수에 붙이는 두 키워드

Async Initializer - An initializer marked async, so creating the value can wait for work and needs await.
한국어: Async Initializer: async로 표시되어 값을 만들 때 기다릴 수 있고 await가 필요한 이니셜라이저

landscape.hook: Can you explain Async Property, Async Throws and Async Initializer in English?

dialogue.title: Why does this property need await?
dialogue.setting: A code review about async getters

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why does Xcode ask for `await` when I read `score`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because `score` is an async property. Its getter can suspend, so you read it with `await`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I see. My `Profile` line shows the same error.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is an async initializer. Creating the value can wait, so write `await Profile()`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I wrote `try await p.score`, but the compiler warns me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: This getter does not throw, so `try` is not needed. Remove it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh, I mixed it up. When do I use async throws, then?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: When the work can fail, like loading a file. A getter can be async throws, too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can an async initializer be async throws as well?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Then the caller writes `try await Profile()`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. So an async property is read-only?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. It only has a getter, so keep the work small.
You need await to read an async property.
